title: The local ring of a scheme-theoretic fibre is a quotient of the local ring
statement: Let $g:Y\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $y\in Y$ and $t=g(y)$, let $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ be the local rings (structure-sheaf stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]), $\mathfrak m_t$ the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{T,t}$, $\kappa(t)=\mathcal O_{T,t}/\mathfrak m_t$ [def-weil-residue-field], and $g^\sharp_y:\mathcal O_{T,t}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ the stalk map of $g$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Let $Y_t=Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre with first projection $p:Y_t\to Y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], and let $y'\in Y_t$ be the unique point with $p(y')=y$. Then the stalk map $p^\sharp_{y'}:\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal O_{Y_t,y'}$ is surjective and its kernel is the ideal $\mathfrak m_t\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ generated by $g^\sharp_y(\mathfrak m_t)$. Hence $p^\sharp_{y'}$ induces a ring isomorphism $\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_t\mathcal O_{Y,y}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{Y_t,y'}$ sending the class of each element $z$ to $p^\sharp_{y'}(z)$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma Tag 0HA1 (lemma-local-ring-fibre), first isomorphism; its proof reduces to the affine case and Algebra, Remark Tag 0H9M (remark-local-ring-fibre)

proof.text: Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $T$ containing $t$, and an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of the open subscheme $g^{-1}(V)$ containing $y$. Such neighbourhoods exist by the local affine condition in [def-pc-scheme], applied also to the open subscheme. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be the section map of the restricted morphism. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] this restricted morphism is $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$. Write $\mathfrak p\subset A$ and $\mathfrak q\subset B$ for $t$ and $y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the germ maps identify $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ with $A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ with $B_{\mathfrak q}$. These are identifications through the original affine opens, not newly chosen local rings.

The field identification $\kappa(t)=A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ respects the map from $A$. Indeed the germ identification in step 1 is a local-ring isomorphism, so preserves the unique maximal ideal; taking its quotient gives that field identification. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification], in $V$ the canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to T$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\to\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. Its image is $t$, so it factors through $V$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] with opens $U\subset Y$, $V\subset T$, and the whole $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$: it identifies $W=p^{-1}(U)\subset Y_t$ with $U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, compatibly with the first projection. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$, where $C=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and its projection to $U$ is induced by $j:B\to C$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. The point $y'$ exists uniquely by the homeomorphism clause of [def-pc-scheme-fibre]; it lies in $W$.

source.place: Tag 0HA1, affine reduction; Tag 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product), Tags 01I4/01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes, lemma-fibre-product-affines); Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves)

proof.text:
Let $\mathfrak Q\subset C$ be the prime of $y'$ in $W$. The affine-stalk identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identify $\mathcal O_{Y_t,y'}$ with $C_{\mathfrak Q}$. The germ formula and composition rule of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-stalk-map-composition] identify the actual projection stalk map with
$\theta:B_{\mathfrak q}\to C_{\mathfrak Q}$, $b/s\mapsto j(b)/j(s)$: on the germ of $b$ it is the germ of $j(b)$, and a ring map sends the inverse germ of $s$ to the inverse germ of $j(s)$. This checks the formula on every fraction. Likewise $g^\sharp_y$ sends $a/u\in A_{\mathfrak p}$ to $\varphi(a)/\varphi(u)\in B_{\mathfrak q}$. Locality of these stalk maps [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] gives $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$ and $j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\mathfrak q$: a germ of a section is in the maximal ideal exactly when its numerator lies in the point's prime; units map to units, while maximal-ideal elements map into the maximal ideal.

source.place: Tag 0HA1 and Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves); Tag 01HY (lemma-morphism-into-affine-where-point-goes); Sheaves Tag 008M (lemma-compose-f-maps-stalks)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-local-ring-natural-iso] to the commutative-ring map $\varphi:A\to B$, the prime $\mathfrak p$, the fibre ring $C$, and its prime $\mathfrak Q$. Its contracted prime is $\mathfrak q$ by step 3. Its displayed map $\theta$ is precisely the actual projection stalk map just computed, including its action on fractions. That node gives surjectivity of $\theta$, kernel $\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak q}$, and the induced isomorphism $B_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak q}\to C_{\mathfrak Q}$ sending the class of $b/s$ to $j(b)/j(s)$. No finite-type, flatness, Noetherian or closed-point assumption is needed by that node.

Finally [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] identifies $\mathfrak m_t$ with $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$. Under the stalk map of step 3 each fraction $a/u$ with $a\in\mathfrak p$, $u\notin\mathfrak p$, maps to $\varphi(a)/\varphi(u)$, a multiple of $\varphi(a)/1$, since $\varphi(u)\notin\mathfrak q$. Conversely every generator $\varphi(a)/1$ with $a\in\mathfrak p$ is the image of $a/1\in\mathfrak m_t$. Thus the ideal generated by the image of $\mathfrak m_t$ is exactly $\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak q}$. Transport the surjectivity, kernel and quotient isomorphism of step 4 through the germ isomorphisms of steps 1 and 3. Every $z\in\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is represented by a fraction $b/s$; the fraction formula in step 4 therefore says that the induced isomorphism sends its class to $p^\sharp_{y'}(z)$, as asserted.
